text: Daily Journals page is automatically created each day and is the default landing page
quote: Every day at midnight a new Journals page is created with that day's date, making it easy to see when you've added what information.

text: Opening Logseq always starts you on the Journals page
quote: Every time you open Logseq, you start on the Journals page.

text: Type [[ ]] to create or link to another page, forming bidirectional wiki-links
quote: Type `[[]]` to create or reference any other page. You can also make a new page in the search bar. - Type `(())` to reference a block on any page.

text: Type (( )) to reference/transclude an individual block on any page
quote: Type `[[]]` to create or reference any other page... Type `(())` to reference a block on any page.

text: Simple {{query}} syntax lets you query your knowledge base for matching content
quote: Simple queries by using `{{query }}`, the format is something like this: {{query Something you're looking for}}

text: Queries can ask questions of your knowledge base (and, in future, the outside world)
quote: Queries are for asking questions from your knowledge base and the outside world (in the future).

text: Third-party plugins can be searched, installed, updated, and removed from a Marketplace
quote: Extends the functionality of logseq with third party tools ... third-party plugins from the Marketplace, can be searched, installed, updated and removed.

text: Plugins not in the Marketplace can be sideloaded via 'Load unpacked plugin'
quote: Click on `Load unpacked plugin` to load plugins that are distributed outside the marketplace.

text: A local HTTP API server can be enabled to give external tools access to your graph
quote: local HTTP server to access logseq's graph ... Enable HTTP APIs server in `Features > HTTP APIs server`

text: The local HTTP server supports authorized external access to the underlying database
quote: we developed the local HTTP server to support external access to the database through authorization.

text: Pages can be individually marked public via a publish:: true property for selective publishing
quote: By default no pages are public. Individual pages can be marked as public with the property `publish:: true`.

text: Export data in multiple formats including text, HTML, OPML, PNG, EDN, JSON, and Markdown
quote: The Logseq Export feature allows users to export their data in various formats, including text, HTML, OPML, PNG, EDN, JSON, and standard Markdown.

text: Graphs can be exported in a Roam Research compatible format
quote: Export the graph in Roam Research compatible format.

text: A whiteboard-style spatial canvas lets you place notes, shapes, drawings, embeds, and connectors together
quote: Put thoughts from your knowledge base as well as new ones next to each other on a spatial canvas together with shapes, drawings, website embeds and connectors.

text: Sync keeps up to 10 graphs updated across Desktop, Android, and iOS
quote: Syncs up to 10 graphs between Logseq Desktop, Android, and iOS.

text: Graph sync is end-to-end encrypted so the vendor cannot read it
quote: Yes, your graph is end-to-end encrypted.

text: A logseq:// URI scheme supports quick capture of short text/links from browser bookmarklets or CLI
quote: Quick capture for short text and links. Can be added as a bookmark link to modern browser or opened from command line shell

text: The logseq:// protocol lets third-party apps invoke actions inside Logseq
quote: Logseq provides a protocol `logseq://` to allow third party applications to invoke actions within Logseq.

text: Community-maintained documentation exists for the Logseq plugin API
quote: This is a community-driven documentation for Logseq plugin APIs.

text: Publishing a graph produces a standalone single-page web application
quote: This feature publishes a graph as a [[Publish Web]], single page application (SPA).

text: Top-level blocks can be converted into their own page (and back) by tagging with #Page
quote: Blocks that have a page as a parent i.e. usually top-level blocks can be converted to a page and back to a block easily. To convert this block to a page, simply tag the block with `#Page`.

text: Logseq is a privacy-first, open-source knowledge base
quote: Logseq: A privacy-first, open-source knowledge base
